thread:
incident-bot: Paging @oncall-jay: Canary failure alarm: 5xx spike on /v1/generate from canary group 'canary-eu-2' after deploy 2026-03-15T10:20Z. Error ratio ~18% over 2m. Logs attached. :warning:
oncall-jay: Picking this up. On my way to laptop. Can anyone confirm recent deploy/flag changes?
emily: I launched a small canary for 2026-03-15 release (commit 9f3b2a1) at 10:18Z. No feature flags touched in that change, only runtime batching tweak.
raj: Seeing similar in logs: OOMs from runtime-worker-3 and 503s from proxy. Stack: "kv cache allocation failed" in inference runtime.
mike: +1. Metrics: latency up and 5xx up specifically for token counts >1024. Canary traffic skewed because test queries include long-context eval.
oncall-jay: Good context. If it's memory regression, we should kill the canary and pop the flag to reduce traffic to that variant. Can we toggle traffic or do a rollback?
emily: Canary traffic is controlled by the rollout flag `rollout/canary-eu-2`. I can flip it to 0% from console.
raj: If we kill the flag we avoid broader impact but existing pods may still serve in-flight requests. Recommend also scaling down canary backend pool.
oncall-jay: Do it. Emily, flip flag. Raj, scale down canary pool. I'll page SRE pager and CS.
emily: Done: `featureflag set rollout/canary-eu-2 0` -> response: success. :white_check_mark: 
raj: Scaling down: `kubectl scale deployment runtime-canary-eu-2 --replicas=0` -> pods terminating. 3 pods drained, errors drop.
deploy-bot: Canary traffic reduced to 0%. Automatic fallback to stable model group 'stable-eu-1' triggered.
oncall-jay: Observability: 5xx rate dropping, tail latency returning to normal. Can we confirm root cause before we re-enable any canaries?
emily: Reproduced locally with the canary image + long inputs. The batching tweak increased memory per-request when KV cache hot paths hit bigger seq_len. Looks like a bad allocation path in the new kernel selection.
raj: Quick mitigation options: 1) revert the single commit 9f3b2a1, which should restore previous batching behavior, or 2) patch runtime to guard allocation. Revert is fastest.
oncall-jay: Agreed. We need minimal blast radius ASAP. Emily — can you open a revert PR and push for hotfix? Raj and I will prepare rollback plan.
emily: Opening PR: `git revert -m 1 9f3b2a1` -> PR #4521 created titled "revert: revert batching tweak causing KV allocation regression". Requesting expedited review.
product-sam: Heads-up: CS reported two customers on canary with long-context usage hitting errors. CS needs messaging if we do broader revert.
cs-liz: Confirmed — Customer A (acme.ai) reported failed requests around 10:22Z, Customer B (finserve) intermittent. We flagged both and offered short-term routing to stable. They are OK for now but want update.
qa-olivia: Quick test plan: run long-context smoke on the revert image, focus on >1024 tokens and KV-heavy prompts. Will run on staging.
oncall-jay: After PR approval, we do a hotfix single-commit revert to canary first, then roll to stable if green. Raj, deploy plan?
raj: Plan: 1) merge PR -> create canary deploy (controlled traffic 1%) 2) run smoke 10 test queries, 3) if green, promote to 100% stable. If any regressions, rollback immediately with `kubectl rollout undo` and re-enable previous stable. I'll standby.
emily: PR merged at 10:33Z. Deploy initiated.
deploy-bot: Hotfix deploy started: image redwood/runtime:9f3b2a1-revert -> canary-eu-2 (1 pod) at 10:34Z.
qa-olivia: Smoke run results: 10/10 long-context queries passed, latency ok. No OOMs observed.
raj: Promoting to stable now. `kubectl rollout status deployment/runtime-stable -w` -> rollout complete. No new crashloops.
oncall-jay: Monitoring for 15m. Early telemetry looks good. 5xx back to baseline.
cs-liz: Messaging update: Notified impacted customers with "We've reverted a recent change and restored normal service; monitoring continues." They acknowledged.
product-sam: Logging a customer-impact note for postmortem. Requesting severity: minor-to-medium due to short outage and targeted customers.
emily: Quick root-cause note: batching tweak changed kernel selection for long sequences causing sudden KV cache growth and oom. Revert avoids the new path until we patch and add an allocation guard.
oncall-jay: Action items: emily to submit follow-up PR with guard + unit tests, raj to add extra e2e long-context coverage, qa to add regression test into CI, cs to follow up customer comms. We'll schedule postmortem tomorrow.
emily: Filed follow-up issue #988: "kernel-selection allocation guard + long-seq e2e".
raj: Handoff: oncall-jay to oncall-next at 10:50Z. Leaving notes in PagerDuty and runbook.
oncall-jay: Handing off to @mike for overnight watch. Summary: reverted commit 9f3b2a1, canary scaled down, stable promoted, customers notified, monitoring nominal.
mike: Taking over. Thanks team. Will escalate if any regression pops up. :thumbsup: 
incident-bot: Incident closed to on-call at 10:45Z by oncall-jay. Postdeploy hotfix successful.
product-sam: Please add follow-up owners and ETA for fix into the postmortem.
cs-liz: I'll call the impacted customers tomorrow to confirm no remaining issues.
qa-olivia: Adding regression test to CI pipeline now.
emily: Will include perf benchmarks for long sequences in the PR.
mike: Noted, monitoring alerts quiet. I'll mark as stable and add to tomorrow's incident retro agenda.
